correctness.rationale: Checked domain n>=3, 1<=b<=r, actual closed-neighborhood payoff. Strict mutual improvement iff both agents lie in monochromatic triples, yielding exact run criterion. Proved n/k via distinguished-blue-run double counting and the run polynomial via inclusion-exclusion. Proved endpoints and no holes of integration support via the k-run intervals, covering b=1, b=r, and n=3 boundary cases. Maximum integration min(n,3b) is attained by blue-short placements. A standalone exact-rational script directly tests opposite-color swaps, not merely the run criterion, for all 35,103 colorings in 55 (n,b) cases n<=15 and reproduces exact polynomial coefficients, total counts and support. Enumeration alone is not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full manuscript of Bilò et al. (2022) proves general existence and efficiency bounds and supplies a cycle price-of-anarchy witness, without stating an exact coefficient-by-integration equilibrium count. This finding proves a structural if-and-only-if for all vertex colorings, its exact three-term run generating polynomial, and full support. These jointly resolve strictly more information than extrema alone. The previously documented result for vacancy-based unilateral jump equilibria has the same extremal ratio, but a different move rule and does not imply swap equilibrium counts. Searches in published research records, primary manuscripts, and relevant combinatorial terms revealed no stronger covering census; this is evidence of noncoverage in inspected sources rather than proof of global priority.
residual_risks: Previously unindexed or unpublished cyclic-word counts may implicitly encode the same coefficients; search is not proof of global novelty.
The original 2022 existence arguments could have unstated elementary corollaries; this work distinguishes full polynomial and support from those already-known qualitative conclusions.
No independent audit or external mathematical validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The full profile-count distribution by integration gives strictly more information than general efficiency bounds for a central canonical spatial network. Exact numbers E(n,b), attainable support, and the integration polynomial allow quantitative analysis of equilibrium multiplicity and welfare at each population imbalance. The result closes a natural family-level census and explains the key structural role of short runs; not a single arbitrary instance, a renamed known bound, or a finite table recheck. The exact price-of-anarchy ratio is a derived byproduct, not used by itself to claim novelty.
